traceability.evidence:
Key implementation files and their linkage to the story:
1) ESLint rule implementation - File: src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - JSDoc: - @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION - @req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE - Defines RuleModule `rule` with: - meta.type: "problem" - meta.docs.description: "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches" - meta.messages.missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}." (clear UX message identifying which annotation is missing) - meta.schema for options: object with optional branchTypes: string[] (uniqueItems) - create(context): - Calls validateBranchTypes(context) from ../utils/branch-annotation-helpers. - If validateBranchTypes returns a listener (object with Program), returns it directly: handles invalid configuration early. - If it returns an array `branchTypes`, iterates each type and registers a handler for that AST node type: - For each branch node, if type === "SwitchCase" and node.test == null, returns early (default case is ignored). - Otherwise calls reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef). - JSDoc on create and handlers explicitly reference 004.0 story and REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION / REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE. - This implements the core rule enforcing annotations on configured branch node types and handling config errors.
2) Branch helper implementation (detection, association, parsing, config) - File: src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts - DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES: - Value: ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase", "TryStatement", "CatchClause", "ForStatement", "ForOfStatement", "ForInStatement", "WhileStatement", "DoWhileStatement"] as const - JSDoc: @req REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA – defines which branches are considered significant by default, covering if/else, try/catch, switch cases, and loops (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION + REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA). - validateBranchTypes(context: Rule.RuleContext): Branch scope configuration and validation - Reads const options: any = context.options[0] || {}. - If Array.isArray(options.branchTypes): - Uses inner helper isInvalidType(t) { return !DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.includes(t as BranchType); } - invalidTypes = options.branchTypes.filter(isInvalidType) - If invalidTypes.length > 0: - Defines ProgramHandler(node): for each invalid type `t`, calls context.report({ node, message: `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(", ")}` }) - Returns { Program: ProgramHandler } (listener used by the rule) - Else returns options.branchTypes as BranchType[]. - If branchTypes is not an array, returns Array.from(DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES). - This matches the story’s REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and invalid configuration behavior: unsupported branch types cause an ESLint error with a clear message listing allowed values. - gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node): Comment association and parsing support - For SwitchCase: - Reads const lines = sourceCode.lines and const startLine = node.loc.start.line. - Iterates from startLine - PRE_COMMENT_OFFSET upwards while lines[i] match /^\s*(\/\/|\/\*)/. - Collects comment lines and returns them joined with spaces. - This handles inline/preceding comments for case branches, satisfying REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION and switch-specific nuance. - For other nodes: - const comments = sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) || []; - Returns comments.map(c => c.value).join(" "). - Associates leading comments with branches in a generic way. - getBranchAnnotationInfo(sourceCode, node): Annotation parsing - const text = gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node). - const missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text); - const missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text); - Determines indentation from sourceCode.lines[node.loc.start.line - 1].match(/^(\s*)/)?.[1] || "". - Computes insertPos via sourceCode.getIndexFromLoc({ line: node.loc.start.line, column: 0 }). - Returns { missingStory, missingReq, indent, insertPos }. - This directly implements REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING. - reportMissingStory(context, node, { indent, insertPos, storyFixCountRef }): - If storyFixCountRef.count === 0: - Defines insertStoryFixer(fixer) that inserts `${indent}// @story .story.md\n` before [insertPos, insertPos]. - Calls context.report({ node, messageId: "missingAnnotation", data: { missing: "@story" }, fix: insertStoryFixer }). - Increments storyFixCountRef.count. - Else: context.report without fix. - Provides clear error and auto-fix for missing @story, aligning with UX and Error Handling criteria. - reportMissingReq(context, node, { indent, insertPos, missingStory }): - If !missingStory: - Defines insertReqFixer(fixer) inserting `${indent}// @req \n` before [insertPos, insertPos]. - Reports with messageId "missingAnnotation" and data { missing: "@req" }, including fix. - Else: reports missing @req without fix (because story is also missing). - reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef): - Uses getBranchAnnotationInfo to determine missingStory/missingReq. - Builds actions array with entries for story and req, each including a flag and function. - Iterates actions and invokes reportMissingStory / reportMissingReq as needed. - Because this is called per branch node, it automatically supports nested and complex control flow structures (REQ-NESTED-HANDLING) and does so in O(number of branches) time (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION).
3) Tests for the branch rule behavior - File: tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - Header: - Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION – explicitly tied to verifying enforcement behavior. - Uses ESLint RuleTester: - const ruleTester = new RuleTester({ languageOptions: { parserOptions: { ecmaVersion: 2020 } } } as any); - runRule(tests) => ruleTester.run("require-branch-annotation", rule, tests). - Valid test cases (showing correctly annotated significant branches): - Switch-case with annotations: - code: switch (value) { // @story ... // @req ... case 'a': break; default: break; } - IfStatement annotated with line comments: - `// @story ...\n// @req ...\nif (condition) {}` - For loop annotated with block comments. - Try/finally with annotations before try. - CatchClause with its own preceding annotations. - Do-while, for-of, for-in, while loops all with proper annotations. - Switch-case with inline annotation and default case without annotations (valid, due to check for SwitchCase.node.test == null for default case). - Configurable scope tests: - With options: [{ branchTypes: ["IfStatement"] }] a switch is not enforced. - With options: [{ branchTypes: ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase"] }] only these branches are enforced. - Confirms REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING, and REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE for positive cases. - Invalid test cases (core functionality, user experience, and error handling): - Missing annotations on if statement: - code: `if (condition) {}` - Expected ESLint errors: two entries with messageId "missingAnnotation" and data { missing: "@story" } and { missing: "@req" }. - Expected output auto-fix inserts `// @story .story.md` above if, exercising fixer behavior. - Missing @req on a for loop with only @story present, verifying detection of partial annotations and @req-specific fix. - Missing @story on while loop with only @req present, verifying @story detection and fix placement. - Missing annotations on switch-case, including variant with a blank line before case – tests rely on fallback scanning behavior for comments near the case, covering edge conditions in comment association. - Missing annotations on do-while, for-of, for-in, and try/catch blocks, verifying all DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES are enforced. - Configurable scope invalid-configuration case: - options: [{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }] - Expects an error whose message matches /should be equal to one of the allowed values/. - This verifies the configuration error reporting path from validateBranchTypes. - All messages use the `missingAnnotation` template, providing consistent and clear error wording, aligning with **User Experience** and **Error Handling** criteria.
4) Tests for helpers (configuration behavior) - File: tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts - Header JSDoc: - Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE – focuses on configuration behavior. - Tests: - No options: validateBranchTypes(context) returns DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - Valid options: with branchTypes ["IfStatement", "ForStatement"], validateBranchTypes returns exactly that array. - Invalid options: with branchTypes ["UnknownType", "Foo"]: - validateBranchTypes returns an object with Program handler. - Invoking Program(fakeNode) causes context.report to be called once for each invalid type, with messages containing `Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values:`. - Confirms configuration validation and error path required by REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and invalid configuration behavior described in the story.
5) Rule documentation - File: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md - Describes the purpose: "Ensures that significant code branches (if/else, switch cases, loops, try/catch) have `@story` and `@req` annotations for traceability." - Explicitly links to story and requirements: - @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION – Detect significant code branches for traceability annotations. - @req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE – Allow configuration of branch types for annotation enforcement. - Details behavior: checks comments immediately preceding branches and requires both `@story` and `@req`. - Options section documents `branchTypes` with: - Default values: full DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES list. - Allowed values: same list. - Invalid values error message: `Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values.` - Examples: - Correct code: if with both @story and @req. - Incorrect code: unannotated branch. - Invalid configuration: branchTypes with "InvalidType" and resulting error description. - This satisfies the **Documentation** acceptance criterion: clear explanation, configuration, and annotated examples.
6) Plugin integration - File: src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes "require-branch-annotation" among other rules. - Dynamic loader loads each rule module from ./rules/${name} and adds to rules map. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps: - "traceability/require-branch-annotation" to "error". - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() returns a config where `rules` is populated using TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES, so require-branch-annotation is enabled with severity error in both `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict`. - This fulfills the "Rule integrated into plugin configuration presets" part of the Definition of Done.
7) Test execution - package.json scripts: - "test": "jest --ci --bail". - Commands executed via tools: - `npm test` → runs Jest across all tests, including tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts and tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts. - `npm test -- --verbose --runTestsByPath tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts` → runs rule-specific Jest tests in CI mode with verbose flag. - The tool output shows Jest invoked with these parameters and no reported non-zero exit codes or errors at the tool layer, consistent with tests passing for this rule.
8) Traceability annotations - Implementation files, tests, and docs all contain JSDoc @story and @req references pointing to docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and relevant requirement IDs (e.g., REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE). This strongly indicates intentional implementation aligned with this story.
Coverage vs story acceptance criteria: - Core Functionality: Implemented and tested – rule detects missing annotations on all significant branch types (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, loops) and reports missing @story/@req. - Quality Standards: Uses ESLint RuleModule, RuleTester, schema validation, and per-node visitors; no obvious performance or correctness anti-patterns. - Integration: Works on a broad set of branch nodes and is fully integrated into plugin index and configs. - User Experience: Error message clearly states which annotation is missing; auto-fixes provide suggestions on exactly what to insert and where. - Error Handling: Invalid configuration is detected via validateBranchTypes and produces clear configuration errors; branches such as default switch cases are intentionally excluded, aligning with significance criteria. - Documentation: Dedicated rule doc with behavior description, configuration options, and annotated examples.
traceability.notes: Story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented. The `require-branch-annotation` rule and its helpers enforce @story and @req annotations on significant code branches (if/else, loops, switch cases, try/catch) with configurable scope, clear error messages, and auto-fix support. Tests validate behavior across many branch patterns and configuration scenarios, including invalid configuration. Documentation describes the rule, configuration, and examples. The rule is integrated into the plugin’s recommended/strict configs. Together, this satisfies all acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done for this story.
